statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail sits at 13% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

What changed in the last hour is real and not a re-pricing of the same standing headline. Lebanese media reported a second round of Israeli airstrikes overnight, on the Ali Taher Ridge in southern Lebanon at roughly 23:07 UTC - the same area where the Hezbollah drone attack wounded three Israeli soldiers on Saturday. The IDF has not officially confirmed those strikes. At around 04:23 UTC Defence Minister Israel Katz said "no account on any front will remain unsettled" and promised to defend soldiers and citizens forcefully, and at about 05:29 UTC the IDF named a second senior Hezbollah commander, Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din of the Badr regional division, as killed in Saturday's Deir al-Zahrani strike. Hezbollah's own promised response is still undelivered.

So Stress moves 70% to 71%. That single point is bought by a new escalation round, not by the clock. The previous hour deliberately halted a 24-hour mechanical climb from 45% to 75% that a fully closed market never justified, and that correction stands: the live cross-asset set is still not a high-70s configuration. NQ September futures closed 30,141.75, about 2.7% below their 30,975.50 52-week high; VIX is 14.25 and fell 2.60% on Friday; the 2-year and 10-year both richer on the week at 4.15% and 4.63%. Only crude expresses the geopolitical premium, with WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52 after a roughly 5% week.

Confidence holds at 70% (solid): the evidence set is complete and primary-sourced, but the price leg is a Friday carry-forward that cannot be refreshed until the restart.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 13% maps to EA_ON for both instruments. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item this hour is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME Globex restart is the single checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window is anchored to it at 22:00-01:00 UTC (00:00-03:00 Berlin). Forecast Tail steps from 19% at 20:00 UTC to 20% at 21:00 UTC and 24% across the reopen, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) from 21:00 UTC through 03:00 UTC Monday before easing back to 19% and green. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment a whole weekend is priced at once: two rounds of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, an explicit Israeli vow to settle scores, a US naval blockade still shutting the Strait of Hormuz, and a crude supply deficit - against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it.

No US macro release lands inside the next 24 hours. Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first genuinely high-impact print. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and nothing here is a trade instruction.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail low at 13% and status green, but a second overnight round of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon and Katz's vow that "no account will remain unsettled" nudge Stress to 71% - with Hezbollah's retaliation still undelivered, the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart is the one checkpoint that matters
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first fifteen forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 70% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour. NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, day range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed as of 14 August; the 52-week range is 22,961.50-30,975.50, which puts NQ roughly 2.7% below its 52-week high. QQQ closed 731.07, -1.00 or -0.14%, day range 728.32-734.39 against a 555.60-748.65 52-week range, about 2.3% below the high (Yahoo Finance). VIX 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, 52-week range 13.38-35.30, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42% on the day, about +5% on the week) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation, both richer on the week from 4.20% and 4.68% the prior day.

That set is internally conflicting, and conflict is a Stress input rather than a Tail input. Index futures are near - not at - 52-week highs, implied volatility is priced for calm on a 14 handle, duration is bid rather than offered, and only crude is expressing the geopolitical premium. Nothing in it is aligned into a one-way equity structure, and none of it can be aligned into one while the venue is shut.

What actually changed this hour. The Lebanon front escalated a second time overnight rather than merely persisting. Lebanese media reported Israeli airstrikes on the Ali Taher Ridge at roughly 23:07 UTC Saturday - the same ridge from which Hezbollah's pre-dawn explosive-drone attack seriously wounded three Israeli soldiers - and the IDF has not officially confirmed them. At about 04:23 UTC Defence Minister Israel Katz said "no account on any front will remain unsettled" and vowed to defend soldiers and citizens forcefully. At about 05:29 UTC the IDF named a second senior Hezbollah commander killed in Saturday's raids: Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din, alias Abu Hassan Alaa, of Hezbollah's Badr regional division, struck at Deir al-Zahrani. Saturday's strikes on Ansar and Deir El Zahrani killed 11 including three children and two women, with 19 wounded, the deadliest since June's de-escalation. Hezbollah's promise that the attacks would be "met with what they deserve" remains undelivered.

That is why Stress takes one point, from 70% to 71%, and why the point is defensible where a further mechanical drift would not be. The previous hour deliberately broke a 24-hour ratchet in which Stress climbed monotonically from 45% to 75% across a market that never quoted once; that correction stands, and this hour is not quietly rebuilding it. A new strike round plus an explicit ministerial vow is new information; the passage of another Sunday hour is not.

Offsetting factors are named rather than ignored. The Lebanon front has a visible diplomatic channel: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun framed the strikes as a "clear message" aimed at the US-sponsored framework negotiations, and an eighth round of direct Israel-Lebanon talks is scheduled for Rome early next month. Escalation with a live off-ramp is a different risk from escalation without one.

On Hormuz, the standing configuration is unchanged and the weekend added rhetoric rather than transmission. The strait has been effectively closed by Tehran since late February and the US naval blockade remains in force; the IEA warned this week that reopening is becoming more pressing as stockpiles draw down, the UAE reported two of its tankers attacked in transit on Thursday, and Iran-Oman talks on a commercial-shipping framework remain unfinished. At about 02:06 UTC an Iranian parliamentary official, Ebrahim Azizi, mocked President Trump's Hormuz sovereignty claim as "endless bluffing." Two things cap how much of this belongs in Tail: the sovereignty rhetoric is legally impossible and already discounted, and Brent at $88.52 is far below the $126 March peak, so this market has absorbed a much larger version of the same shock and mean-reverted from it.

Calendar. The next seven days contain no CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP or FOMC decision. Verified against Trading Economics this hour: Empire State and NAHB on Monday, Housing Starts and Building Permits on Tuesday at 12:30 UTC, the July FOMC minutes on Wednesday at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey on Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday at 13:45 UTC. Retail earnings dominate the corporate week - Home Depot Tuesday, Target, Lowe's, TJX and Analog Devices Wednesday, Walmart and Alibaba Thursday - so there is no megacap or semiconductor print capable of creating index-level one-way structure inside the window. The two largest scheduled catalysts sit just outside the seven days and are therefore not in the events array: the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August, with Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed Chair on 28 August, and Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 report on 26 August.

Why Tail 13%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements and repeated extension. With no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe, and the last observed session was a quiet -0.15% drift inside a 254-point range. dominantMode stays mixed - conflicting cross-asset signals with no dominant direction.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 06:00 UTC Saturday to 05:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours, and the action was EA_ON, the status green and dominantMode mixed for all 24. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 13%. Stress is what moved: 48, 48, 50, 51, 52, 53, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75 and then 70. The first 23 of those are a near-monotonic 27-point climb across a market that never quoted once - each hour re-priced the same standing headlines slightly higher rather than re-testing them - and the final slot is the deliberate correction that stopped it, taken after re-verifying Friday's cross-asset marks against primary sources. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 70% as those marks were checked hour by hour, which is the part of the track that was earned. The lesson carried into this hour: a Stress point has to be bought by new evidence, and this hour it was.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 05:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first seven hours after it are inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 15 of 24 slots, drifting 13% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 20% at 21:00 UTC and 24% across the reopen before easing through 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 04:00 UTC Monday. The forecast action is WATCH and the forecast status yellow from 21:00 UTC through 03:00 UTC. Stress rises gently from 71% to a 78% peak into the reopen - genuinely unpriced weekend risk does compound while the venue is shut, and this weekend added a second strike round to it - then eases to 73% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Confidence decays from 70% to 63% as Friday's marks age, then recovers to 73% after the restart, a larger recovery than the decay because a live price path is the single missing input. The last nine slots switch to event/whipsaw for a thin opening auction that has to absorb a full weekend at once. No US macro release falls inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first high-impact catalyst.
